items.title: Crisis-induced hybrid learning, cognitive offloading, and generative AI reliance among Pakistani CS undergraduates
items.abstract: Purpose In spring 2026, geopolitical tensions prompted the Pakistani government to mandate full online instruction (10 March–3 April 2026), followed by a hybrid schedule for the rest of the semester. This shift is treated here as an externally imposed crisis context for AI adoption, not as a natural experiment. No pre-crisis baseline or control group was available. The study characterises generative AI (GenAI) adoption patterns and the psychological antecedents of AI dependency among undergraduate computer-science (CS) students during this window. Three hypotheses, grounded in the reviewed literature, structured the analysis. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was administered across Pakistani higher education institutions (HEIs) in April–May 2026. Of 360 responses collected, two incomplete records were removed, and a thirteen-criterion data-quality screen was ap-plied, yielding N = 299. Fourteen constructs were operationalised from UTAUT, Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), Self-Determination Theory (SDT), and the AI Anxiety Scale (AIAS). Block-entry OLS regression and bootstrapped mediation (5,000 resamples) tested the hypotheses; ANOVA and Spearman correlations supported descriptive analysis of adoption patterns. Findings Adoption was near-universal (>99%), with 45.2% of respondents reporting ≥ 31% of submitted work directly AI-generated. A three-block OLS regression explained 54.6% of variance in AI dependency. Cognitive offloading was the strongest predictor (β = 0.41, p < 0.001), followed by procrastination (β = 0.23, p < 0.001), extrinsic motivation (β = 0.17, p = 0.002), and intrinsic motivation as a protective factor (β = −0.13, p = 0.013). Bootstrapped mediation confirmed procrastination partially mediates the extrinsic motivation–dependency path (ab = 0.201, 95% BC-CI [0.122, 0.289]). Originality/value To our knowledge, this is among the first studies to survey GenAI dependency during an active government-mandated crisis disruption in South Asian higher education. Contributions include a multi-theory construct battery adapted for a crisis context, a thirteen-criterion response-quality protocol, and evidence that habituated cognitive offloading and extrinsic motivation are the primary drivers of AI dependency in this context.

items.title: CroissantMiner: Automated Extraction and Validation of Croissant Metadata for ML Datasets
items.abstract: Croissant has emerged as a standard for machine-readable dataset metadata, yet populating its fields remains labor-intensive and requires careful reading of accompanying dataset documentation. We present the first benchmark enabling end-to-end evaluation of metadata extraction aligned with a community-standard schema. The benchmark comprises 602 papers, including 102 with human-validated gold annotations and 500 with LLM-generated silver annotations, covering the full Croissant schema with both core and Responsible AI (RAI) fields. Using this benchmark, we evaluate a range of extraction systems spanning frontier models, open-weight models, and agentic architectures, under a two-tier evaluation framework that combines rule-based scoring with an LLM judge selected via human audit. We find that single-pass extraction consistently outperforms the four agentic architectures we evaluate: across backbones, these decomposed variants achieve lower accuracy than a single full-context pass. The largest gap appears on long-form RAI fields, which require synthesizing and interpreting information scattered across a paper rather than copying it from a single location, a setting where current systems remain far from reliable. We release the benchmark, evaluation code, judge audit, a live demo, and a leaderboard open to new systems.

items.title: Cross-lagged associations of work schedules, commuting, and bedtime screen use with weekday sleep duration in Japanese workers
items.abstract: Objectives Work schedules, commuting, and off-job routines shape the time available for sleep on workdays, yet longitudinal evidence on which of these factors are most consistently associated with weekday sleep duration remains limited. Methods We surveyed Japanese adults at two points: August 2022 (T1) and November 2022 (T2). The analysis included 508 regular workers who did not work night or shift schedules. Participants reported their weekday sleep duration, working hours, commuting time, work start time, household chore time, and pre-sleep screen use at both times. Results Using cross-lagged panel modeling, we found that longer commuting time (β = –0.064, p < 0.05) and earlier work start time (β = 0.072, p < 0.05) at T1 were prospectively associated with shorter sleep duration at T2. We observed reciprocal prospective associations between pre-sleep screen use and sleep duration: a shorter time from last screen use to sleep at T1 was associated with shorter sleep duration at T2 (β = –0.091, p < 0.05), and shorter sleep duration at T1 was also associated with a shorter time from last screen use to sleep at T2 (β = –0.091, p < 0.05). Weekly working hours did not show a significant prospective association with sleep duration. Conclusions Work start time and commuting time, rather than total working hours, may be more relevant to weekday sleep duration among regular workers, although the observed associations were small. Workplace scheduling and commute-related policies, alongside guidance on evening screen use, may be relevant occupational health targets.

items.title: CVIF: A Criticality-Driven Visual Intervention Framework for Geometric Diagram Understanding in MLLMs
items.abstract: Despite significant progress in visual tasks by Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), geometric diagram understanding remains challenging due to the presence of sparse visual cues and ambiguous symbol-primitive associations. MLLMs may therefore rely on textual priors, producing interpretations that conflict with visual evidence. We introduce the training-free Criticality-Driven Visual Intervention Framework (CVIF), an inference-time method that localizes critical layers and executes visual interventions during the transition from evidence aggregation to semantic decoding. At these layers, a Geometry-Constrained Local Relation Reconstruction (GCLR) module selects and weights vertex-centered visual evidence, while an Adaptive Visual Steering Operator (AVSO) redistributes attention mass toward the selected tokens. Experiments on PGPS9K and PGDP5K show that CVIF raises Overall F1 from 77.85 to 85.58 and from 75.23 to 82.84, respectively, establishing a novel inference-time visual intervention paradigm.

items.title: Cyber Security Awareness and Responsible AI Adoption: A Mediation Analysis of AI Risk Perception
items.abstract: Abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into organisational workflows has introduced unprecedented cybersecurity challenges, necessitating a deeper understanding of how users perceive and respond to AI-related risks. This study investigates the mediating role of AI Risk Perception in the relationship between Cyber Security Awareness and Secure AI Usage Behaviour. Drawing on Protection Motivation Theory and employing a cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 300 respondents across diverse industries using a structured questionnaire measuring three latent constructs. Mediation analysis, conducted using the PROCESS macro with bootstrap confidence intervals, revealed that Cyber Security Awareness has a strong positive effect on AI Risk Perception (path a: β = 0.712, p < 0.001), which in turn positively influences Secure AI Usage Behaviour (path b: β = 0.444, p < 0.001). The direct effect of Cyber Security Awareness on Secure AI Usage Behaviour remained significant (path c′: β = 0.413, p < 0.001), while the indirect effect through AI Risk Perception was also significant (β = 0.316, 95% CI [0.229, 0.404]). These findings support partial mediation, indicating that AI Risk Perception accounts for approximately 43.3% of the total effect. The results underscore the importance of integrating cybersecurity education with AI risk awareness programmes to foster responsible AI adoption.

items.title: Cyber-Physical Systems and IoT: Edge Analytics, Predictive Maintenance, and BIM/DT Interoperability in Construction 6.0
items.abstract: This chapter examines how cyber-physical systems, IoT, edge analytics, and Digital Twins collectively shape the technological foundation of Construction 6.0. It highlights the integration of embedded sensors, real-time edge processing, and multilayer architectures that enable low-latency decision-making for structural health monitoring, safety alerts, energy management, and equipment diagnostics. The chapter emphasizes human-centric predictive maintenance, where Artificial Intelligence-driven modelsranging from classical Machine Learning to deep learning and hybrid physics-informed approachesoperate alongside explainability mechanisms to support technician oversight and trust. Interoperability emerges as a central challenge, addressed through standards such as ISO 19650, Industry Foundation Classes, building Smart Data Dictionary, Global Standards One Electronic Product Code Information Services 2.0, Message Queuing Telemetry Transport /Sparkplug B, and Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture, ensuring consistent data exchange across Building Information ModellingIoTArtificial Intelligence ecosystems. Security, ethics, and governance frameworks grounded in zero-trust principles further reinforce resilient cyber physical systems deployments. Overall, the chapter presents an integrated roadmap toward intelligent, interoperable, and human-aligned construction environments.

items.title: Cybersecurity Challenges in Online Banking: Best Practices for Protection a Comprehensive Analysis of Threats and Mitigation Strategies in the United States Banking Sector
items.abstract: The rapid digitalization of banking services in the United States has fundamentally transformed how financial institutions operate and interact with customers. While online banking offers unprecedented convenience and accessibility, it simultaneously introduces complex cybersecurity challenges that threaten both financial institutions and consumers. This article examines the current landscape of cybersecurity threats facing online banking systems, analyzes the impact of these challenges on digital banking adoption, and presents comprehensive best practices for protection. Through systematic analysis of recent literature and industry data, this study identifies key vulnerabilities in online banking infrastructure and proposes an integrated framework for cybersecurity risk management that addresses both technological and human factors in the digital banking ecosystem.

items.title: CYMEDSEC Cybersecurity Performance in Remote Patient Monitoring Systems in a Live Hospital Setting: Protocol for an Observational Study
items.abstract: Background: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) systems based on the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) technologies are increasingly integrated into chronic disease management and telemedicine pathways. Despite their widespread adoption, cybersecurity performance, system resilience, and user behavior in real-world clinical environments remain underexplored. Existing evidence is fragmented, often limited to laboratory simulations or vendor-driven assessments, leaving a critical gap in understanding how cybersecurity risks across the full life cycle of RPM systems deployed in health care settings. Objective: This study aims to systematically analyze the cybersecurity posture, system resilience, and user behavior across the full life cycle of IoMT-enabled RPM systems in a real-world hospital and home-care environment. The study aims to generate empirical evidence on how technical safeguards, operational workflows, and human factors influence cybersecurity risks during procurement, integration, deployment, routine use, and decommissioning of these platforms. Methods: This observational study will analyze 2 independent RPM systems used for chronic disease monitoring in a real-world hospital setting. The assessment framework includes (1) system-log analytics to evaluate authentication events, device connectivity, update and patch management, and anomalous behaviors; (2) a controlled phishing simulation targeting health care professionals to assess susceptibility and response patterns; (3) an evaluation of update management processes and vendor-hospital interactions; (4) measurement of cybersecurity awareness and practices among patients and health care professionals using validated instruments; and (5) mapping of vulnerabilities across all life cycle phases, from procurement to decommissioning. Although the study includes cybersecurity training, preassessments/postassessments, and controlled phishing and update-management scenarios, these activities are part of the observational framework and are not designed as experimental interventions that have an impact on the clinical aspects of patient care. Quantitative data will be analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative insights from operational workflows will be integrated to contextualize system performance. Ethical approval has been obtained from the institutional ethics committee. Results: The CYMEDSEC (enhanced cybersecurity for networked medical devices through optimization of guidelines, standards, risk management, and security by design) project received funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe program (grant 101094218) and started on November 1, 2024. Ethical approval was obtained on December 18, 2025, and institutional authorization on January 29, 2026. Patient enrollment is scheduled to begin on April 1, 2026. At the time of paper submission, no patients were recruited. Data analysis will begin after completion of patient involvement, with results expected before the project end date in October 2027. Conclusions: This study will provide real-world evidence on the cybersecurity performance of IoMT-enabled RPM systems, capturing the interplay among technical safeguards, operational processes, and human factors. Findings are expected to support the development of security-by-design approaches, inform procurement and regulatory frameworks, and guide the safe integration of connected medical devices into routine care within the framework of the CYMEDSEC research project.

items.title: D3.2 - MultiX perception system enablers v2 Focus on MPS system design
items.abstract: This deliverable reports the second stage of the development of the MultiX Perception System (MPS) within MultiX WP3. While D3.1 laid the foundations of the ISAC framework by designing individual perception enablers, D3.2 consolidates these enablers into functioning sensing technologies and packages them as Measurement Sensing Processing Functions (m-SePFs). These are self-contained, interface-defined build- ing blocks that can be deployed and reused within the MultiX architecture. Perception enablers. D3.2 extends the technical results of D3.1 across channel modelling, waveforms, and multiband/multistatic processing. As part of Task 3.1, a physics-consistent Electromagnetic (EM) framework generates multiband Radar Cross- Section (RCS) statistics for complex targets, validated against full-wave simulation across Frequency Range 1 (FR1), Frequency Range 2 (FR2), and Frequency Range 3 (FR3). The Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS)-based framework for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarm sensing is extended to realistic, partially- observable multipath conditions, adding association-map estimation, joint position/velocity tracking, and silent- intruder detection. Regarding multiband sensing, an unambiguous multiband Doppler/velocity estimation method working across multiple frequency bands is proposed. On multistatic and multiband processing (Task 3.2), the deliverable introduces a CF-mMIMO-based multistatic respiration sensing enabler validated on a 64-antenna testbed, a hierarchical coherent/non-coherent imaging algorithm for composite moving targets, and a full set of sensing-driven tracking filters (Kalman, Particle, Alpha- Beta) extending the mmWave ISAC detection introduced in D3.1. Regarding Task 3.3, on energy-efficient Artificial Intelligence (AI) sensing architectures, a fully event-based, spiking-neural-network ISAC receiver architecture is introduced, replacing the conventional OFDM receiver chain to substantially reduce the energy consumption of edge sensing nodes. An initial multiband measure- ment campaign is also reported, targeting the training of GenAI models for channel frequency response recon- struction across frequency and spatial gaps. Sensing processing functions. Building on these enablers, D3.2 specifies eight m-SePFs at the most ad- vanced stage of development: coherent multiband ranging, timing/frequency/phase offset calibration, coherent multistatic imaging, RCS and micro-Doppler estimation, inter-band sensing integration, respiration sensing from distributed antennas, mmWave ISAC-enabled tracking of dynamic objects, and inter-band unambiguous Doppler estimation. Compared to D3.1, each function’s specification is enriched with more granular input/out- put fields, new operational parameters (processing type, response time, output data size), and an explicit mapping to the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) A–D sensing measurement abstraction levels. System integration. D3.2 defines how the m-SePFs are deployed and connected within the MultiX architec- ture across the MPS, the MultiX Perceptive 6G-RAN Controller (MP6RC), and the Data Access and Security Hub (DASH) through the Network Sensing Control and data interfaces. D3.2 also details the system design choices governing how individual enablers combine into a coherent MPS: dependency chains, coherent/non- coherent/hybrid processing, processing-split placement, and band/node selection. The resulting capabilities are mapped onto the two MultiX Proof of Concepts (PoCs): the Multi-layer Network Digital Twin for Indus- trial Manufacturing (PoC 1) and Contact-free eHealth Monitoring at Home (PoC 2). This establishes the link between WP3 and the validation activities of WP4, which will be carried forward in D3.3. Ethical aspects. As some WP3 experimental activities involve the collection of sensing data from human subjects, the deliverable summarises the ethical safeguards adopted, including informed consent and Data Protection Impact Assessment procedures, in compliance with the MultiX Ethics deliverable D7.1.

items.title: Daily job crafting with generative artificial intelligence: Implications for work meaningfulness and engagement
items.abstract: As Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen-AI) becomes embedded in daily work, understanding how employees proactively engage with these tools to shape their work experiences is increasingly important. Building on self-determination theory and the job crafting literature, this study introduces the concept of daily Gen-AI-driven job crafting: employees' self-initiated use of Gen-AI to modify their daily job demands and resources. We examine whether Gen-AI-driven job crafting is associated with daily work engagement through psychological need satisfaction and work meaningfulness. We employed a daily diary design with 149 UK-based full-time employees (M age = 36.7, SD age = 10.4; 63.8% male) who used Gen-AI at work daily or multiple times per day over ten consecutive workdays, incorporating a brief open-ended question to examine whether employees experienced their Gen-AI use as intentional work modification. Quantitative results showed that the dimensions of Gen-AI-driven job crafting (augmenting instrumental resources, augmenting social resources, augmenting challenging demands, and automating hindering demands) were differentially associated with daily work engagement through need satisfaction (autonomy, competence, relatedness) and, in turn, work meaningfulness: the competence pathway received the most consistent support, while the relatedness pathway was the most limited. Open-ended responses were consistent with intentional work modification, for instance, automating hindering demands was framed as a strategic reallocation of cognitive resources toward more valued work rather than simple workload reduction. Together, these findings suggest that Gen-AI may function as a bottom-up work design tool associated with daily need satisfaction and engagement.

items.title: Data-Driven Personas for Survey Simulation: Insights into Simulation Alignment Across Data-Access Regimes
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for public opinion research by enabling early prediction of survey responses, potentially reducing the cost and time of traditional surveys. However, many existing steering approaches rely on target-domain human data for fine-tuning or prompting that is costly to collect and raises privacy concerns. In this paper, we study demographic group-level survey simulation, where personas induced from heterogeneous, anonymized public behavioral data condition agents that simulate responses of individuals from specific demographic groups. We examine whether representative personas can be induced from diverse sources and analyze how the domain, scale, and granularity of the source data affect survey simulation alignment. We find that personas induced from out-of-domain sources rarely outperform simulations conditioned only on basic demographic information, largely due to population mismatch. However, when personas are accurately assigned to the target demographic groups, alignment improves substantially. Finally, personas induced from target-domain survey data generalize better as more survey question history becomes available, suggesting that richer behavioral evidence enables more stable persona trait inference that transfers to better unseen questions simulation alignment.

items.title: Defense-in-Depth for LLMs: Evaluating Memory Gates Against Activation-Induced and Memory-Induced Sycophancy
items.abstract: Long-term memory allows Large Language Models (LLMs) to maintain personalized context across interactions, but retrieved user history can induce memory-induced sycophancy, causing models to favor stored user beliefs over objective evidence. Existing defenses primarily operate on retrieved context and are rarely evaluated jointly with internal behavioral bias. We introduce a $2 \times 2$ defense-in-depth framework separating internal activation steering from external memory handling. We extract sycophancy steering directions from 100 paired prompts and evaluate four open-weight models across 10 steering coefficients and five memory-defense configurations on MemSyco-Bench (answers for all 1,550 items; defense conditions judged on a fixed 250-item subsample), with three LLM judges. Three of the five configurations are new (rewriting every memory, a Router Gate that keeps, rewrites, or drops each memory, and dropping all memory); the other two are MemSyco's baselines. Selective Router Gate filtering preserves substantially more of MemSyco's average accuracy than complete memory removal, and this separation persists when the models are steered toward sycophancy. On Llama 3.1 8B with Router Gate, mild inverse steering ($α= -1.5$) lowers judge-averaged sycophancy from 35.80% to 31.32% while average accuracy moves from 43.99% to 43.31%; this reduction has the same direction under all three judges but is not statistically significant (paired $p = 0.08$ to $0.63$ on 149 items). External memory filtering is the part of the design that holds up; our data do not show that inverse steering adds to it.

items.abstract: An electromagnetic (EM) digital twin gives mobile robots wireless situational awareness but depends on material conductivities that change with the environment. Online calibration faces initialization sensitivity and measurement travel costs. We demonstrate a vision-language model (VLM)-guided framework using a Unitree G1 robot and NVIDIA Sionna, with two VLM calls: material classification maps visible materials through ITU-R P.2040 to conductivity priors for Sionna's gradient descent on accumulated received signal strength (RSS) measurements; waypoint planning selects the next measurement location online using residual RSS calibration error and image coverage. In a real indoor scenario, the framework achieves a normalized mean absolute conductivity error of $1.74\times10^{-4}$ within 20 m of travel; random initialization never converges, while random waypoints require over twice the travel.

items.title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent-Based Chatbot for Al-Hikmah University
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the delivery of academic support services through intelligent conversational systems capable of providing timely and accurate responses to users. Traditional methods of obtaining information within higher education institutions often rely on manual interactions with administrative staff, resulting in delays, increased workload, and limited accessibility outside official working hours. This study presents the design and implementation of an intelligent-based chatbot for Al-Hikmah University to automate responses to students' academic enquiries. The chatbot was developed using a retrieval-based architecture integrated with Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to understand user queries and retrieve relevant responses from an institutional knowledge base. The system was implemented using React.js for the frontend, Node.js and Express.js for the backend, MongoDB as the database management system, and Google's Gemini API to enhance conversational intelligence. Functional and usability evaluations were conducted using representative student queries covering admission, registration, course information, tuition fees, examinations, and academic regulations. Experimental results demonstrated that the chatbot provides 98% accurate responses with low response within one to two seconds latency while remaining available twenty-four hours a day. The proposed system improves accessibility to institutional information, reduces the workload on administrative personnel, and enhances students' overall experience. The study concludes that AI-powered academic chatbots can significantly improve digital service delivery in Nigerian universities and recommends future integration with voice recognition, multilingual support, and student information systems.

items.title: Design and Preliminary Validation of a ROS2-Based Autonomous Mobile Robot for AI-Assisted Airport Security and Terahertz Screening
items.abstract: Airport security screening is largely concentrated at fixed checkpoints, leaving limited opportunities for continuous monitoring within terminal areas. This paper presents the design and preliminary validation of a ROS2-based autonomous mobile robot intended to provide an additional security layer through real-time object detection, tracking, mapping, navigation, and future integration of non-ionizing terahertz-(THz) imaging. The prototype integrates an NVIDIA Jetson Orin, Intel RealSense D415 camera, RPLidar-A1, Arduino-based motor control, and a mobile platform. ROS2, RViz2, Navigation2, and YOLOv11 were used to combine perception, visualization, motion control, and system monitoring. Laboratory tests demonstrated live indoor mapping, detection of people and objects, persistent tracking identities, target tracking, motor operation, and wireless access. A survey of 54 respondents examined passenger acceptability; half expressed comfort with mobile robotic scanning, while 75.9% believed it could improve airport security. Acceptance depended strongly on non-ionizing operation, privacy protection, transparency, and human oversight. Because the THz camera was not experimentally integrated owing to budget constraints, concealed-object detection remains a proposed capability. The study establishes a functional foundation for future THz-RGB-D-LiDAR fusion, quantitative performance evaluation, cybersecurity assessment, and controlled airport trials. It also identifies key technical, ethical, regulatory, and human-factor requirements for responsible deployment in crowded, safety-critical airport terminal environments.

items.title: Design and Usability
items.abstract: This chapter traces the evolution of usability from its focus on physical measurements to addressing more complex cultural considerations, advocating for design as an organic set of conditions rather than static endpoints. It challenges designers to move beyond controlling users and toward discovering new design possibilities through unexpected uses and manipulations. The chapter identifies three waves of usability development. First-wave usability focused on physical experience through ergonomics and human factors design. Henry Dreyfuss pioneered measuring design against human body dimensions, while Niels Diffrient’s Humanscale attempted generalities. However, these standards revealed inherent biases based predominantly on Western white male statistics, with problematic historical connections including Ernst Neufert’s work for the Third Reich. The concept of “extreme users”—those with varying abilities, sizes, or ages—emerged to combat these biases, though empathy suits still fail to capture emotional and cognitive dimensions. Second-wave usability introduced human-centered design as cognitive study. Donald Norman’s The Design of Everyday Things established foundational concepts bridging the “gulf of knowledge” (knowledge “in the head” versus “in the world”) and the “gulf of execution.” Affordances became central—including perceived, hidden, anti-, and false affordances. Perceived affordances focus on what the user perceives can be done, whether or not that feature exists; hidden affordances remain undiscovered by users; anti-affordances intentionally prevent actions (like speed bumps or hostile architecture’s spikes preventing homeless people from resting); false affordances create the illusion of action without the effect. The perception at the center of the use of affordances relies on schemas—mental constructs from cultural experiences— which allow users to apply previous knowledge to new situations. Third-wave usability examines cultural and contextual experiences in life-centered design. Design anthropology emerged within this wave to better understand how cultural attitudes affect design usability, challenging colonial mindsets in both anthropology and design practice. Elizabeth Tunstall’s Decolonizing Design advocates for designers to question biases, “listen first,” and cede power to communities, shifting from extractive data-gathering toward mutually beneficial, reciprocal relationships that acknowledge design’s role in shaping future cultures.

items.title: Design of a highly efficient graphene-coated ultra-wideband solar thermal absorber for renewable mining energy applications using artificial intelligence optimization
items.abstract: Although many technologies have advanced in electricity production, their carbon footprint remains a crucial factor in selecting the most sustainable option. Solar energy provides a promising solution, as it is a clean and renewable resource harnessed directly from the sun. Multi-layer type thermal absorbers are considered the most effective structures, and their efficiency can be further enhanced with the incorporation of advanced materials such as graphene and MXene. In the current study, the solar absorber is fabricated using Cr-Fe₃O₄-InSb materials, with a thin graphene film added to enhance overall thermal performance. The design features two square structures with a cylindrical resonator inserted at the center. The proposed structure achieves an impressive thermal absorption rate of 93.28% through a broad wavelength range of up to 2800 nm. Specifically, the structure can be configured to achieve a thermal absorption rate of 90.9%, 93.32%, and 94.72% for UV-Vis-NIR regions while maintaining these rates across the respective ranges: 90.9% in the ultraviolet, 93.32% in the visible, and 94.72% in the NIR, with the polarization-insensitive property applicable for incidence angles from 0 to 80 degrees. To extract precise performance values based on regression analysis for varying layer heights, machine learning techniques for a 0.25 test size and the R² value reach above 0.98. As a thermal energy innovation, the proposed absorber can be utilized in various thermal processes, including water heaters, cookers, solar ponds, fuel production, coffee roasters, swimming pool heating, and more.

items.title: Designing for Organisational Capability: From Intended Outcomes to Sustained Performance
items.abstract: Why can an organisation invest in people, learning and technology, meet its performance targets, and still depend on particular individuals to keep work moving? Successful outcomes can conceal missing information, unclear decision authority and disconnected processes when capable employees compensate for weaknesses in the arrangements surrounding their work. Designing for Organisational Capability: From Intended Outcomes to Sustained Performance examines how organisations can deliberately design the conditions through which required outcomes are produced, sustained and adapted. Building on From Workforce to Organisational Capability, it develops an outcome-first approach that connects people, work, information, authority, learning, support and technology around the performance the organisation needs to achieve. A continuing illustrative service-team case carries the argument from defining the intended outcome to tracing work, strengthening interfaces and creating the conditions for workplace application. The paper then examines the relationship between human judgement and AI, how evidence makes performance evident, and how organisations build the capacity to adapt as operating conditions change. The discussion draws on research into training transfer, informal learning, organisational design, generative AI and dynamic capabilities, alongside NIST’s AI Risk Management Framework. It distinguishes these research foundations from the Capability Design applications developed within the paper. Written for leaders, learning and development professionals, work designers and organisational practitioners, the whitepaper offers a basis for examining whether investments have established dependable capability and what must work together for intended outcomes to become sustained performance. Part of the Capability Excellence™ Whitepaper Series.

items.title: Developing Requirements for Standards in the Field of Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The research is devoted to the issue of creating a safe and reliable artificial intelligence (AI) system. Objective: to create a clear list of requirements for future standards in the field of ethics of artificial intelligence in order to bridge the gap between theory and practice. Methods: methods of induction and synthesis, comparative analysis and analogy are used. Results: an analysis of the existing guidelines on AI ethics was carried out and it was concluded that it contains mainly general recommendations, without specific technical rules. Possible errors and the reasons for the difficulty of holding potentially responsible parties accountable in the field of AI implementation are presented. A three-component list of requirements for artificial intelligence technologies and the relevant data on the basis of which they are defined has been developed; a step-by-step plan for integrating ethical principles into practical aspects of development and regulation has been proposed. The practical significance lies in offering a framework for national and international regulatory documents that will ensure the safe use of the technology and increase user confidence.

items.title: Developing Sustainable Chemistry with AI
items.abstract: Conspectus Today we are experiencing an unprecedentedly rapid transformation of science, driven by advances in computing and artificial intelligence (AI). At the same time, there are growing cumulative pressures of climate change impacts that not only affect economies but are creating significant societal challenges. The confluence of technology push and environmental–socioeconomic pressures is promoting the development of sustainable chemistry. The link between the transition to sustainability in chemistry and the digital transformation of R&D and manufacturing has been the long-standing focus in our research (Fantke, P.; et al. Chem 2021, 7, 2866 doi: 10.1016/j.chempr.2021.09.012). Sustainability is not a feature of a single chemical product or a process. It is incorrect to talk about “sustainable polyethylene”, as such narrow framing will miss many issues in the more holistic system that not only includes the cradle-to-grave life cycle emission impacts of polyethylene but also considers all aspects of equity, impact on biodiversity, resilience of supply chains, etc. Sustainable chemistry makes sense only as a complex system. An analysis of complex systems requires large amounts of data and the use of appropriate analytical tools, such as advanced machine learning techniques. The chemical industry has been an early adopter of digital technologies, motivated by the inherent complexity of chemical systems and the need for efficiency to stay economically competitive. As early as the 1970s, cheminformatics tools were introduced to support structure–property analysis. In the 1980s, we saw the broad adoption of process modeling and simulation tools for design, scale-up, and optimization of chemical processes, paralleled with developments in the field of process system engineering and control. Today’s digital transition is much deeper; everything from scientific discovery (molecules, materials, and phenomena) to chemical process development, analytical methods and process analytical technologies, and plant operation is being reshaped. This deep transformation includes the development of a radically different approach to data in chemistry. Advances in self-driving laboratories, agentic AI workflows, and digital factories require access to structured, semantically rich data. In this Account, we focus on three key areas of digitalization and AI technologies advancing chemistry and chemical process development toward net-zero targets. First, we discuss how data mining tools are used to analyze the existing value chains and identify opportunities to integrate net-zero feedstocks. When new molecules are introduced, data-driven route planning can be employed to design alternative synthetic pathways, which then need to be rigorously evaluated. Second, we focus on how to use AI to accelerate discoveries in chemistry, including the innovative design of catalysts, rational selection of solvents, and identification of optimal reaction conditions. By leveraging statistical modeling and data-driven optimization, these traditionally time-consuming tasks can now be performed much faster. Lastly, we discuss how to bring these innovations from the laboratory to manufacturing, which also requires advances in process technologies. We show that by leveraging AI agents, process modeling, and knowledge graphs, there is a potential to achieve automated process design and life cycle assessment, removing traditional choke points in scaling technologies and providing timely support for decision-making in early-stage development. In the end, we discuss the current challenges and future perspectives.

items.title: Development and Nationwide Multicentre Evaluation of Guideline-Grounded Large Language Model Chatbots to Support Patient Self-Management and Education in Rheumatology
items.abstract: Patients with rheumatic diseases have persistent information needs that are not fully addressed in routine care. We developed and evaluated guideline-grounded, large language model (LLM) chatbots to support patient self-management and education in rheumatology.Ten disease-specific chatbots based on German guidelines were co-developed and deployed through 13 rheumatology centres and six patient organisations. Chatbot users rated responses and completed a questionnaire. User questions, feedback, and response characteristics were analysed using category-based coding and a six-dimensional LLM-as-a-judge assessment, with LLM-based ratings compared with rheumatologist ratings in random subsets.Between September 2025 and January 2026, 6291 questions were recorded. Thirteen question categories were identified, most commonly disease-specific questions (50.2%), medication and monitoring (37.3%) and diagnostics (28.2%). The chatbots were unable to answer in 263 interactions (4.2%). Of 2671 responses rated by users, 2481 (92.9%) received a positive rating. Insufficient detail was the most common reason for negative ratings (125/190, 65.8%). Among 602 questionnaire respondents, 84.6% reported that the chatbot was easy to use, 84.1% that answers were easy to understand, and 80.2% that it was a useful addition to patient education. In the LLM-based evaluation, 95.3% of answers were rated as completely safe and 79.1% as completely correct. Guideline adherence was assessed separately, with 45.0% rated as fully adherent; agreement with physician assessment was weak.Guideline-grounded chatbots received predominantly positive user feedback in real-world use, while LLM-based evaluation suggested that most responses were safe and correct. User questions and feedback may help guide iterative improvements to source content and patient education materials. Further studies are needed to evaluate educational effectiveness and independently validate response quality and clinical safety.

items.title: Development of a master of science in digital health program at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, Tanzania: a mixed-methods curriculum development study
items.abstract: Background The rapid expansion of digital technologies is transforming health systems and creating increasing demand for a workforce with competencies in health informatics, data science, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, digital health governance, and implementation. However, digital health training remains fragmented in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), including Tanzania. This study describes the systematic, evidence-based process used to develop an MSc Digital Health program at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS), Tanzania. Methods A mixed-methods curriculum development approach was undertaken, comprising document review and benchmarking, a quantitative stakeholder survey, qualitative interviews with alumni of the MSc Health Information Management program, and a stakeholder consultative workshop. Nine higher-education and competency-framework sources were reviewed to identify gaps and emerging competency domains. A structured survey was administered to 48 stakeholders purposively selected from government, non-governmental, private-sector, and start-up organizations. Qualitative data from alumni interviews and open-ended survey responses were analyzed thematically using manual coding by two independent coders. A two-day consultative workshop involving 22 stakeholders from academia, professional associations, non-governmental organizations, government, and clinical practice reviewed and validated the proposed curriculum. Results Benchmarking demonstrated substantial variability in digital health curriculum content, with no single program comprehensively covering all priority competency domains. Stakeholders identified AI and machine learning (48.0%) and big data and analytics (41.7%) as prominent emerging technology competencies, while data science and predictive analytics, health information systems and interoperability, cybersecurity and data privacy, and epidemiology and biostatistics were also emphasized. Overall, 81.3% of survey respondents considered digital health competencies highly important to their organizations, while 89.6% indicated willingness to employ MUHAS MSc Digital Health graduates. Qualitative findings emphasized five priority areas: advanced computing and emerging technologies; applied health data science and analytics; health systems architecture and interoperability; experiential learning and program delivery; and governance, cybersecurity, leadership, and professional ethics. Workshop participants endorsed the proposed curriculum and recommended stronger practical learning, field attachment, innovation-oriented projects, and alignment of course content with emerging workforce needs. The resulting program was structured as a two-year, full-time MSc Digital Health program with three specialization tracks: Digital Health Leadership, Digital Health Systems Development, and Health Data Science and AI. Conclusion The MUHAS MSc Digital Health curriculum was developed through an iterative, evidence-informed, and stakeholder-driven process that integrates multidisciplinary digital health competencies with practical, implementation-oriented learning. The approach provides a potentially adaptable model for curriculum development in LMIC settings. Future evaluation should assess program implementation, graduate competencies, employment outcomes, employer satisfaction, and contribution to national digital health transformation.

items.title: Developmental perspectives and improvements for regional Disaster Medicine Services of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation amid current realities
items.abstract: Relevance . The analysis of existing practices regarding the elimination of medical and sanitary emergency consequences has revealed several challenges in the operation of regional Disaster Medicine Services (DMS) of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation. Research-based approaches to DMS further development and improvement are undoubtedly pivotal to improve preparedness within disaster medicine institutions by establishing ad hoc emergency response units capable of efficient medical care provision in case of emergency, including emergency medical care. The study aim is to outline the most promising perspectives for further DMS development and improvement by analyzing the years-long experience in medical care provision to eliminate medical and sanitary emergency consequences in the Russian Federation. Materials and methods . We studied the current regulatory and legal framework of the Russian Federation, research publications, the present DMS across regions, as well as the extensive practical experience of healthcare workers and DMS units in medical care provision within emergency response efforts. The study utilized historical and analytical methods, content analysis, expert assessment, contrastive and systemic analysis, comparison, and scientific synthesis. Results and discussion . Based on the DMS requirements, 10 fundamental conceptual approaches were developed to advance and improve the existing organizational structure across Russian Federation constituents, as well as underpin relevant management decisions regarding the assets and resources. The essence and content of the proposed approaches are elaborated; promising areas for DMS development in constituents of the Russian Federation have been identified. A retrospective analysis of response efforts to medical and sanitary consequences caused by the most critical and high-profile large-scale emergencies with mass sanitary losses in our country has been conducted with regard to the proposed approaches. Conclusion . The principal strategic direction for further development and improvement of regional DMS should include augmented efficiency of the service management system, optimized regulatory, legal, and methodological support, improved organizational and functional DMS and staffing structure across its units, as well as enhanced professional competencies in medical triage among healthcare workers, transformed approaches to logistics and material resource supply, and integrated artificial intelligence, information technologies, software platforms, and decision-support systems into DMS management processes.

items.title: Diagnostic performance of ChatGPT for acute appendicitis compared with the Alvarado score: a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
items.abstract: Acute appendicitis remains the most common cause of acute abdomen and is associated with serious complications such as perforation if not diagnosed promptly. While laboratory tests and clinical findings are essential, their interpretation can be challenging and sometimes misleading. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, has shown promise in supporting clinical decision-making and enhancing diagnostic accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of ChatGPT-5 to predict the likelihood of appendicitis using clinical data, with diagnoses confirmed by histopathology and comparing it to Alvarado score which is most commonly known clinical scoring system to diagnose acute appendicitis. This retrospective comparative study evaluated the performance of ChatGPT-5 in predicting acute appendicitis across two phases. In Phase 1, the model was tested without prior context learning (i.e., without exposure to any previously labeled cases) to simulate real-world use of readily available LLMs. In Phase 2, it was re-tested after exposure to confirmed case outcomes. A structured prompting strategy was applied, incorporating patient demographics, clinical symptoms, laboratory data, and clinical context, with fixed output constraints across all cases. The dataset was divided into 70% (114 cases) for Phase 1 evaluation and 30% (48 cases) for Phase 2 validation. To address potential order leakage- a bias arising when predictions depend on case sequence rather than clinical reasoning- the cases were assessed both with and without randomization. Paired comparisons of sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy between ChatGPT-5 and the Alvarado score were performed using McNemar’s test, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess agreement. In Phase 1, ChatGPT-5 without randomization achieved a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 81.6%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 91.6%, negative predictive value (NPV) of 100%, and overall accuracy of 93.9%, compared with the Alvarado score (sensitivity 67.1%, specificity 92.1%, PPV 94.4%, NPV 58.3%, accuracy 75.4%). In Phase 2, ChatGPT-5 without randomization reached a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 93.8%, PPV of 97.0%, NPV of 100%, and accuracy of 97.9%, comparable to the Alvarado score (sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 93.8%, PPV 96.9%, NPV 93.8%, accuracy 95.8%). Within this retrospective, surgically confirmed cohort with a high clinical suspicion of acute appendicitis, ChatGPT-5 showed high diagnostic sensitivity for excluding acute appendicitis when guided by an optimized prompt, even without prior context learning. Proper randomization of prompt data appears essential to minimize order leakage and to provide a more conservative and reliable estimate of model performance. ChatGPT-5 cannot yet be relied upon to confirm acute appendicitis, given the higher specificity of the Alvarado score, and its diagnostic sensitivity remained largely unaffected by context learning, with only a modest, non-significant gain in specificity. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation in a broader emergency-department population before any clinical implementation.

items.title: DIALER: A Case for Improving Rare-Class Accuracy in Retraining-Free Edge Video Analytics
items.abstract: Edge video analytics with lightweight models is prone to accuracy degradation due to persistent distributional shifts in live video streams. While continuous learning (CL) addresses such data drift, it heavily strains the limited compute resources of edge servers originally provisioned for inference. Our empirical study reveals that emerging vision foundation models (VFMs) offer a practical, retraining-free alternative that delivers high average accuracy with remarkable compute savings. However, VFMs frequently misclassify specific rare classes, which often represent critical objects, as visually similar common classes. We design DIALER, a system that exploits the spare compute cycles freed by retraining-free VFM inference to mitigate rare-class misclassifications. Specifically, DIALER pre-builds multi-stage correction pipelines for dominant rare-to-common confusion pairs offline. At runtime, it routes correction candidates to the corresponding pipelines and executes as many stages as idle GPU headroom permits. Evaluation on four real-world driving datasets shows that DIALER improves rare-class accuracy by up to 14.0% without interfering with real-time VFM inference for multi-stream analytics.

items.title: Differentiable Bit-Widths: Co-optimizing Pruning and Quantization via SVD for Ultra-Efficient LLM Compression
items.abstract: SVD-based pruning and quantization have recently emerged as a promising strategy for the ultra-efficient compression of large language models. In these methods, compression is performed in two stages: components are first truncated, and the remaining ones are subsequently quantized. Although this decoupled pipeline benefits from both pruning and quantization, it requires separate optimization for each stage and fails to fully exploit their balance, which can lead to suboptimal performance under aggressive compression. To address this limitation, we propose a new LLM compression method that co-optimizes pruning and quantization in a unified framework. Our key idea is a differentiable method for learning component-wise bit-widths, allowing less important components to be assigned 0-bit precision and pruned away. Notably, our method performs favorably against two-stage baselines, even when subjected to extreme quantization settings ($1.61$ bits) designed for ultra-efficiency. items.title: Digital Exaptation: The Evolutionary Mechanism of Emergent Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper proposes the theory of Digital Exaptation (디지털 굴절적응) to resolve the foundational debate surrounding emergent reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs). Contemporary artificial intelligence discourse often views higher-order reasoning either as an unpredictable artifact of empirical scaling laws or dismisses it as mere statistical mimicry ("stochastic parrot"). Borrowing from evolutionary biologist Stephen Jay Gould’s concept of exaptation—wherein a trait evolved for one primary adaptive function is co-opted for an entirely novel utility (e.g., feathers evolving for thermoregulation before being exapted for aerodynamic flight)—we argue that reasoning in foundation models is not a teleologically designed objective, but an exaptive structural byproduct of hyper-dimensional statistical compression. By reframing LLM emergence through evolutionary biology, this paper bridges empirical machine learning and the philosophy of mind.

items.title: DIGITAL HUMANITIES AND THE EVOLUTION OF DIGITAL TEXT ANALYSIS IN LITERARY STUDIES
items.abstract: This article provides a comprehensive evaluation of the historical development, methodological frameworks, and contemporary paradigms of digital text analysis within Digital Humanities (DH). Tracing the disciplinary trajectory from early mid-twentieth-century humanities computing – focused on concordance building, lexicography, and foundational stylometry – to the current era of computational literary studies driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP), deep learning, and Large Language Models (LLMs), this paper demonstrates how computational methods reshape literary scholarship. Key analytical frameworks, including distant reading, macro-analysis, sentiment analysis, social network analysis, and co-reference resolution, are systematically reviewed. Furthermore, the study addresses critical epistemological and technical challenges, such as the risk of hermeneutic reductionism, algorithmic bias, and the cross-cultural gap in applying computational tools to low-resource languages. Ultimately, the paper argues for a symbiotic hybrid methodology that bridges computational scale with qualitative close reading, offering a holistic paradigm for future literary research.

Digital Twins, continuously updated through Building Information Management, IoT sensing, and AI analytics enable real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and lifecycle optimization. The chapter highlights foundational frameworks such as the Gemini Principles, ISO 23247, and human-in-the-loop approaches that ensure transparency, trust, and explainability in Digital Twin-driven decisions. Critical challengesincluding cybersecurity vulnerabilities, semantic interoperability, and ethical governanceare addressed through zero-trust architectures, ontology-based data models, explainable Artificial Intelligence, and blockchain-enabled auditability. The chapter further explores how Digital Twins support sustainability and the circular economy via material passports, carbon tracking, and resource-efficient lifecycle strategies. Case studies demonstrate measurable benefits in safety, energy performance, and predictive analytics, positioning Digital Twins as central to human-centric, resilient, and sustainable Construction 6.0 ecosystems.

items.title: Disclosure willingness anthropomorphism and thinking style shape perceived fit and comfort in AI mental health chatbot interactions
items.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) conversational agents are increasingly used for everyday, non-clinical mental-health support, yet little is known about when these exchanges feel fitting and comfortable. We used a laboratory mixed-methods design to examine associations among perceived convenience of interaction (PCI), relational attitude (RA), willingness to self-disclose (WSD), anthropomorphism (AN), perceived fit/comfort (FC), and thinking style in 83 participants (43 rational-dominant; 40 experiential-dominant). WSD showed the strongest unique association with FC. A post hoc reverse model also found a unique FC-WSD association, leaving their temporal order unresolved. AN had no stable direct association with FC, but the WSD-FC association became stronger as AN increased. Group comparisons and continuous Rational-Experiential Inventory (REI) analyses converged: relatively stronger experiential processing was associated with higher AN, whereas relatively stronger rational processing was associated with higher WSD. The group-blind thematic analysis linked disclosure decisions to privacy, control, social distance, functional usefulness, and affective comfort. Together, the findings identify WSD as a key correlate of FC and show that anthropomorphism conditions this association rather than simply improving the interaction. Clear boundaries, controllability, and adjustable relational cues therefore warrant attention in future design research.

items.abstract: This research aims to explore the nature of left-handed children and identify the necessary conditions for their effective preparation for school. The study analyzes the brain activity of left-handed children, specifically their unique characteristics in visual imagery and spatial perception. The research provides a scientific rationale regarding the negative neuropsychological and pedagogical consequences of forcibly retraining left-handed children to use their right hand. Additionally, the author has developed methodological recommendations for developing graphic skills, organizing an ergonomic workspace, and the use of specialized educational tools designed for left-handed students.

items.title: Do Small Language Models Learn to Negotiate? A Controlled Scaling Study of RL-Trained Sellers
items.abstract: LLM agents are starting to own the full customer experience. Soon, LLMs may be selling and buying on behalf of companies and customers respectively. Small models are more cost-efficient at scale, but can reinforcement learning train them into competent sellers? We train four Gemma 4 checkpoints (2.3B to 31B effective parameters) with GRPO on a programmatic utility reward for bilateral multi-issue bargaining, and evaluate every arm on the same 1,152 negotiations against two frontier buyers it never saw in training. With the same learning rate ($10^{-6}$) for every size, the gain of the RL model over its base rises from $+0.001$ at 2.3B to $+0.078$ at 31B. Each size was trained once and the two smallest checkpoints use a different architecture, so we fit no scaling law. Tripling the learning rate, with the same or fewer training steps, improves on the shared rate at every size by $+0.032$ (2.3B) to $+0.081$ (4.5B). In exploratory comparisons with two frontier models run as sellers, the 12B seller trained at the tripled rate scores above both, though its untrained base already scores as high as they do. The 4.5B seller at that rate shows no detectable difference from either and fits on one 48 GB GPU. A further 2.3B arm at ten times the shared rate raises pooled score, but its gain concentrates on the evaluation buyer that shares a model family with the training pool. These results suggest tuning the learning rate before concluding that a small model cannot learn to negotiate, and testing against buyers from more than one model family.

items.title: Domain-adaptive Bengali text summarization: Harnessing transformer-based large language models in closed-set contexts
items.abstract: This work aims to develop a domain-adapted Bengali text summarization model by training and fine-tuning on general and domain-specific datasets with categories such as state, international, and sports. Flan-T5 and mT5 LLMs were trained on the XLSUM Bengali dataset for text summarization, and they were trained on source domains and fine-tuned on the target domains for domain adaptation. In general-domain summarization on the XLSum Bengali dataset, mT5 achieved stronger overall performance than Flan-T5, with ROUGE-1 and BERTScore values of 0.21 and 0.72, respectively. The Flan-T5-XLSUM model outperformed other LLMs, achieving a ROUGE score of 0.79, a BLEU score of 0.13 and a BERTScore of 0.86. A human evaluation involving 28 participants was conducted to assess summary fluency, adequacy, and factual consistency across domains, confirming the qualitative effectiveness of the proposed models. A custom dataset is developed with manually annotated categories for domain adaptation purposes, contributing to domain-specific Bengali data. The ablation study illustrated that pre-training and fine-tuning on domain-specific data significantly enhanced model performance, with Flan-T5 fine-tuned on sports data. Three explainability methods (LIME, SHAP, and BertViz) revealed that geographically and contextually meaningful tokens strongly influenced the domain-adaptive Flan-T5 Bengali summarization model. The adapter-based Flan-T5 architecture enables effective multi-domain fine-tuning with less than 1% of trainable parameters while preserving model performance.

items.title: Driving organizational performance through OHS culture and management in manufacturing SMEs within construction supply chains
items.abstract: Introduction This study examines the relationships among Organizational Culture, Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Management, and Organizational Performance in manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating within construction supply chains in Norte de Santander, Colombia. Methods We collected survey data from 204 employees across 16 manufacturing SMEs and analyzed them using structural equation modeling (SEM). The model evaluated the direct relationships among the three constructs and the indirect effect of Organizational Culture on Organizational Performance through OHS Management. Results The results indicate that Organizational Culture is positively associated with OHS Management and Organizational Performance, while OHS Management is positively associated with Organizational Performance. The bootstrapped indirect effect supports OHS Management's partial mediating role. Discussion These findings suggest that Organizational Culture is associated with performance through two complementary pathways: a direct pathway involving shared values, managerial commitment, communication, and organizational practices, and an indirect pathway involving the institutionalization of OHS management practices. The study contributes to the literature by positioning OHS Management as an organizational mechanism that helps explain how cultural conditions relate to performance outcomes. For manufacturing SMEs linked to construction supply chains, the findings highlight the importance of integrating cultural development with risk prevention, safety training, regulatory compliance, and employee participation. The results should be interpreted considering the cross-sectional design, the use of self-reported data, and the nesting of employees within a limited number of firms.
